race_context: The district: Delaware Community School Corp. (DelCom) serves Delaware, Hamilton, Niles and Union townships in Delaware County northeast of Muncie, including Eaton, most of Albany and a small part of Muncie {wiki_dcsc}. Its schools are Albany, Eaton and Royerton elementary schools, Delta Middle School and Delta High School {wiki_dcsc}{dc_min_260921}. Greg Kile is superintendent and Darin Gullion is assistant superintendent {dc_min_260921}. This guide did not find a verified current enrollment figure.

The board has five members: Jacob Case (president), John Adams (vice president), David Grasso (secretary), Lance Engle and Valerie Alexander {dc_board}. Seats are tied to townships: in 2022 the Delaware, Niles and Union township seats were on the ballot {sp_2022a}. Case and Adams were sworn in for new terms in January 2025 after the 2024 election {dc_min_250106}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the Delaware, Niles and Union township seats, one member each, as in 2022 {in_list}{sp_2022a}. In 2022 Engle filed for another term in the Delaware Township seat; Alice Gillis filed for the Niles Township seat, which Case was leaving; and no one filed for the Union Township seat then held by Trent Fox {sp_2022b}. All three current members whose seats are up — Engle, Grasso and Alexander — are on the 2026 ballot for the Delaware, Niles and Union township seats respectively {dc_board}{in_list}. Only the Delaware Township race is contested.

Party labels: under the 2025 state law allowing school board candidates to list a party, the ballot list shows Jeremy Scott Gard and Valerie K Alexander as Republicans, David M Grasso as an Independent and Lance Joseph Engle as Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Facilities and bonds (2026): the board held hearings April 20 and May 4, 2026 on a project covering playground equipment, roofing and site improvements and the purchase of buses, equipment and technology, to be financed with bonds {dc_bond_notice}. On May 4 the board adopted the project resolution and related bond resolutions after a hearing at which one resident spoke in favor {dc_min_260504}. Earlier bond-funded work included a renovation of Albany Elementary that board members toured in February 2026; the district held a community open house there April 10 {dc_min_260202}{dc_min_260406}.

Budget (2026): the board held a public hearing Sept. 8, 2026 on the 2027 budgets, the 2027-2029 capital projects plan and the 2027-2038 bus replacement plan, with no public comments, and adopted the budget, plans and tax rates 5-0 on Sept. 21 {dc_min_260908}{dc_min_260921}. On Sept. 8 it also approved resolutions to reduce 2026 appropriations and to transfer money to and spend from the rainy day fund {dc_min_260908}.

Enrollment and transfers: the board set enrollment capacities and a priority date for transfer applications in April 2026 and held lotteries in June for transfer spots in Royerton Elementary's kindergarten and third-grade classes {dc_min_260406}{dc_min_260601}.

Academics and curriculum: board members praised elementary IREAD-3 results in April 2026 {dc_min_260406}. In 2026 the board approved world language and business textbook adoptions and, on May 4, purchases of elementary textbooks from McGraw Hill ($315,734.17) and middle school textbooks from HMH ($52,098.50) {dc_min_260420}{dc_min_260504}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of these races.
